title: Threshold sign multiplication identity
statement: Let $a\in\mathbb R$ and let $s\in\{ -1,1\}$. Define the sign of a real number $u$ to be $1$ when $u\ge0$ and $-1$ when $u<0$. Then $a\,\operatorname{sign}(a)s=|a|s$.
